$comment: Declarative desired state for the factory. `factory apply` makes the live
Paperclip instance match this file; it is the only sanctioned way to mutate
the control plane. The ad-hoc scripts/apply-*.sh are superseded evidence.
IDENTIFIERS: everything is resolved by stable name (company name, project
name, agent name, issue identifier). No database UUID appears in this file.
A rebuilt instance re-resolves cleanly; a copied UUID would silently target
the wrong row or nothing at all.
${FACTORY_ROOT} expands to the repo root of the running CLI, so the same
config is correct from the primary tree and from a worktree.

pins.$comment: Asserted, not installed. `factory status` fails if any drifts.

$comment: enableIsolatedWorkspaces MUST be true. With it off the server DELETES
executionWorkspaceId / executionWorkspacePreference / executionWorkspaceSettings
from issue create and update and returns 200 with the unchanged issue
(services/issues.js:5312, :5610, :5850); it is also the dispatch-time gate
at services/heartbeat.js:10677. Silent failure, not an error.
enableWorktreeRunExecution MUST be false. Despite the name it is unrelated
to agent execution workspaces: it arms only when the Paperclip SERVER runs
inside a worktree (PAPERCLIP_IN_WORKTREE). Enabling it here changes server
behaviour for no benefit.

instructions.$comment: Binds this agent to the compiled instructions/out/AGENTS.engineer.md whose sha256 is pinned by the committed instructions/manifest.sha256. Load verifies the bytes against the manifest; factory apply reconciles the live server copy with exact readback.

$comment: Configured through the adapter's FIRST-CLASS keys.
These agents run on @zhafron/paperclip-omp-adapter (adapterType
omp_local), the external Oh My Pi adapter installed under
~/.paperclip/adapter-plugins. Oh My Pi (OMP) and `pi` are DIFFERENT
products: @paperclipai/adapter-pi-local in node_modules serves pi and
does not run these agents. Reading it to judge these keys is reading
the wrong file — that mistake is what produced the claim that the keys
below are inert.
The adapter builds OMP argv from these keys in dist/server/execute.js:
configFiles -> --config (:187), extensions -> --extension (:189),
pluginDirs -> --plugin-dir (:191), hooks -> --hook (:193),
tools -> --tools (:153), skills -> --skills (:155),
approvalMode -> --approval-mode (:156). extraArgs is appended LAST
(:216), so it is an escape hatch for flags with no key, not the only
route. Nothing is hardcoded.
autoApprove DEFAULTS TO TRUE (:158): with no valid approvalMode the
adapter pushes --auto-approve by itself. Both are set explicitly here
so the value is declared rather than inherited from a default.
The policy overlay and the worktree guard ride on configFiles and
hooks. `--config` overlays are strict, so a missing or malformed
policy is a hard startup error, not a silent fallback to unpoliced
execution.

instructions.$comment: Binds this agent to the compiled instructions/out/AGENTS.reviewer.md whose sha256 is pinned by the committed instructions/manifest.sha256. Load verifies the bytes against the manifest; factory apply reconciles the live server copy with exact readback.

$comment: READ THE ENGINEER'S COMMENT FIRST — the same first-class keys govern.
THE READ-ONLY BOUNDARY LIVES IN `tools`. The adapter emits --tools only
when this key is non-empty (execute.js:132,153) and hardcodes nothing.
Leave it unset and OMP falls back to its own default tool set, which
includes write access — the plan forbids that: the Reviewer's verdict
has to be an observation, not an intervention.
`ast-grep` is NOT a valid OMP tool name and is in the live list; it
would be a fatal CliUsageError at startup. The valid names are read,
grep, glob, lsp, todo, plus the custom paperclip_review.
DISCOVERY IS `--extension`, NOT `--plugin-dir`, so the plugin path goes
in `extensions`. The plugin uses the nested tools/<name>/index.ts
layout, which only the omp-plugins provider reads
(discovery/omp-plugins.ts:248); --plugin-dir feeds a different provider
that globs tools/*.{ts,js} non-recursively and cannot see it.
`env` carries the two model identities paperclip_review reads to prove
the reviewing model is not the producer's family. It is the one
adapterConfig key Paperclip's server validates (envConfigSchema); a
plain string is a valid binding. Without it the tool fails closed and
the Reviewer refuses to review at all.

issues.$comment_objectiveDocument: The immutable objective is the versioned ObjectiveEnvelopeV1 at contracts/objectives/ZEI-1.json. Load verifies its schema, hashes, and issue binding, and renders the document body that factory apply upserts as issue document 'spec' with optimistic concurrency (baseRevisionId) and exact readback. The document is authoritative; the objective changes only by a new revision with new hashes.

$comment: THE FULL STRATEGY, ATOMICALLY. execution-workspace-policy.js:275 resolves
issueSettings.workspaceStrategy ?? projectPolicy.workspaceStrategy
with `??`, NOT a merge. A partial issue strategy therefore REPLACES the
project's and silently drops branchTemplate and worktreeParentDir, landing
the run on branch `ZEI-1-<slug>` inside `/home/lucascoh/X-Bookmarks/.paperclip/worktrees`
— untracked noise in the operator's own repo. Never write a partial strategy here.

issues.$comment_responsibleUser: THE ESCALATION TARGET. On round exhaustion the server hands the stage to reviewEscalationUserId(issue) = responsibleUserId ?? createdByUserId ?? null (issue-execution-policy.js:345). When that resolves to NULL the escalation branch at :681 is skipped entirely and control falls through to `patch.status = in_progress` reassigned to the return assignee — the Engineer. That is the blocked-and-loop state the plan forbids, reached by omission rather than by error. Resolved by operator key, never by UUID.

executionPolicy.$comment_maxReviewRounds: DECLARED HERE BECAUSE THIS IS WHERE THE SERVER LOOKS. resolveMaxReviewRounds(policy) reads policy.maxReviewRounds (issue-execution-policy.js:336) and falls back to DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 3 (:9). The copy under issues[].limits is the factory's own promote-time gate; it is never sent to the server, so declaring the ceiling only there would leave the live instance running 3 rounds while the config appeared to say 2.

$comment: 45 minutes is HARD: it reaches the run as adapterConfig.timeoutSec/maxTime.
$4 is a GATE, not a hard stop: Paperclip budget scopes are company/agent/project
only (POST /api/companies/{id}/budgets/policies — no issue scope), so no
per-issue ceiling exists to set. The factory enforces it by refusing to
promote a run whose reported cost exceeded it. The hard stops behind it are
the Engineer's $40 agent budget and the provider-side OpenRouter cap.
The $5 factory-wide figure is an outer bound and never relaxes this.

operator.$comment: The human who owns the approval stage and every escalation.
